processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process). Solution-treated baseline hardness of the 15Al alloy was 253.4 ± 2.1 HV.
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching. This is the 525 °C / 3 h condition (the sample of interest).

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 15Al alloy at 525 °C for 3 h, a significant amount of β-Mn precipitated (85.8 %), with only a small amount of the α matrix remaining untransformed. The phase map is nearly uniformly β-Mn (green) with only sparse α (red) regions.

phases_present.morphology: precipitated β-Mn forming the majority (matrix) after α→β-Mn transformation
small untransformed α islands (red) within the green β-Mn matrix

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → β-Mn transformation: at 525 °C the β-Mn precipitated rapidly in the 15Al alloy; within 3 h of aging at 525 °C the α matrix was almost completely transformed into β-Mn (85.8 % β-Mn), leaving only small untransformed α regions.
interfaces.interface_notes: For this low-temperature (525 °C/3 h) 15Al condition, the new BCC and FCC Cu-rich interfacial precipitates reported for the higher-temperature/peak-hardness samples are not described; only β-Mn and residual α are resolved.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured using an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and reported as the average.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 3 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness of the 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h was 872.0 ± 21.2 HV, increased from the solution-treated baseline of 253.4 ± 2.1 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize constituent phases and their fractions in the 15Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 3 h (Figs. 4, 15)
characterization_methods.key_findings: After aging at 525 °C for 3 h the 15Al alloy showed 85.8 % β-Mn with only a small amount of untransformed α matrix; figure_004 (a1/a2) phase maps show nearly uniform green β-Mn with sparse red α islands.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in the 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h (Fig. 7)
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 525 °C/3 h panel shows an emerging β-Mn matrix with a red 'Untransformed α' arrow marking remnant α, consistent with the near-complete α→β-Mn transformation.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h, the formation of β-Mn raised the hardness from 253.4 HV (solid-solution state) to 872.0 HV, demonstrating the strong hardening effect of the β-Mn phase (b0040).
The β-Mn volume fraction of the 15Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 3 h was 85.8 %, with only a small amount of α matrix remaining untransformed (b0040).

In the 15Al alloy the α matrix was almost completely transformed into β-Mn within 3 h of aging at 525 °C, whereas the 17Al and 19Al alloys required 6 h and 10 h at 550 °C respectively — the increase in Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics (b0065).
The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness in the 15Al alloy was about 525-600 °C (b0038), so the 525 °C/3 h condition lies within the ultra-hard window (872.0 HV).

According to figure_007 the 525 °C/3 h SE micrograph of the 15Al alloy shows a mostly uniform transformed matrix crossed by a curved boundary, with a red 'Untransformed α' arrow and a green β-Mn arrow, indicating the near-complete α→β-Mn transformation at this condition.
